<user_request>
模型：Grok Video Generation，6 段 × 8 秒，MEDEO 拼接为 48 秒。
核心原则：全片禁止任何可读文字、字母、数字、符号、字幕。无语音旁白。书本仅在 00:00 竖向打开一次，在 00:48 竖向合上一次。中间所有场景通过"穿过纸幕层"实现转换，禁止翻页、禁止黑场。六段首尾帧严格共用：clip1 尾帧 = clip2 首帧，clip2 尾帧 = clip3 首帧，clip3 尾帧 = clip4 首帧，clip4 尾帧 = clip5 首帧，clip5 尾帧 = clip6 首帧。clip1 首帧与 clip6 尾帧共用 @Image1，形成完美循环。
视觉风格 — Paper-Cut Light Box / Shadow Box： 全片采用纸雕灯与竖向隧道书（vertical tunnel book）美学。书本竖立放置于深色桌面上，打开后内部是 5-6 层平行排列的厚卡纸剪影（heavy cardstock silhouettes），每层如同剧场幕布，彼此间隔 3-5 厘米，形成强烈景深。每层卡纸背后有独立背光源（backlight），使剪纸边缘透出暖金或冷蓝轮廓光（glowing halos around cut edges），正面则呈现深影剪影。人物、动物、建筑均为平面剪纸，但多层叠加后产生立体纵深感。卡纸表面可见真实纤维纹理与激光切割边缘厚度。
色调：外层（clip1-2）冷蓝月夜、银白、午夜蓝；内层（clip3-4）暖金琥珀、烛光色；深层（clip5-6）冷蓝转暖金，最终回归封面暗调。
镜头：纵深推进（dolly-in / push-in），从书外逐层向最深处穿透。穿过某层纸幕时，该层如剧场幕布向两侧轻柔卷开/分开/变薄，露出后一层背光轮廓，不可生硬切换。
Step 0 — 封面图 @Image1：ChatGPT Image-2 生成 [哈利波特] 竖立实体书封面。深红色压纹皮革，烫金标题，哥特巴洛克装饰边框，书脊有厚度。书本竖立闭合，置于深色桌面，背景暗黑，仅封面有微弱烛光反射。无其他文字。
Step 1 — 首尾帧图 @Image2（clip1 尾帧 = clip2 首帧）：ChatGPT Image-2 生成竖向隧道书第一层——月夜禁林剪纸。厚卡纸剪影，前景是层叠纸云与纸树枝，一只白色折纸猫头鹰站在枝头，羽毛由剪纸鳞片构成。冷蓝色背光从纸层后方透出，云层边缘泛银白光。整体如纸雕灯般，剪纸边缘有透光轮廓。无文字。
Step 2 — 首尾帧图 @Image3（clip2 尾帧 = clip3 首帧）：ChatGPT Image-2 生成竖向隧道书第二层——九又四分之三站台剪纸。厚卡纸剪影，哥特式拱廊层层排列，纸质蒸汽火车头剪影位于中层，烟囱正喷出纸卷烟雾（烟雾为半透明剪纸层）。暖黄色背光从火车窗与拱廊后方透出，人影提箱剪影走向火车。前景纸层边缘有暖金透光。无文字。
Step 3 — 首尾帧图 @Image4（clip3 尾帧 = clip4 首帧）：ChatGPT Image-2 生成竖向隧道书第三层——魁地奇球场剪纸。厚卡纸剪影，环形看台层层环绕，追球手骑扫帚剪影位于中层，金色飞贼为发光纸球。暖金背光从看台后方强烈透出，形成戏剧性剪影对比。前景有纸云飘浮。无文字。
Step 4 — 首尾帧图 @Image5（clip4 尾帧 = clip5 首帧）：ChatGPT Image-2 生成竖向隧道书第四层——大礼堂剪纸。厚卡纸剪影，长桌纵向排列，纸质烛火以背光透光形式呈现（火焰为镂空剪纸，后方暖光穿透），天花板悬挂纸星星。暖琥珀背光，纸尘在光束中漂浮。无文字。
Step 5 — 首尾帧图 @Image6（clip5 尾帧 = clip6 首帧）：ChatGPT Image-2 生成竖向隧道书第五层——禁林深处剪纸。厚卡纸剪影，高大树木层层林立，一只折纸牡鹿（守护神）位于中层，银白色背光从其纸身透出，撞碎前方纸网。冷蓝背光为主，牡鹿周围有银白透光轮廓。无文字。
Clip 1 — 竖书开启与第一层月夜禁林（00:00-00:08） 首帧锁定 @Image1。尾帧锁定 @Image2。
00:00-00:03 画面：竖立闭合书本置于暗黑哥特书房桌面，封面 @Image1 朝上，仅有微弱环境光勾勒书脊轮廓，氛围神秘静谧。
00:03-00:08 画面：书本竖向缓缓打开（像翻开一本立体画册），封面与封底向两侧展开，内部第一层厚卡纸幕布如剧场幕布般从中央向两侧舒展立起。第一层呈现月夜禁林剪纸——层叠纸云、纸树枝干、一只折纸猫头鹰站在枝头。冷蓝色背光从纸层后方亮起，云层与树枝边缘透出银白轮廓光，纸雕灯效果显现。镜头从书外缓慢纵深推进，向第一层靠近。03 秒书本开始竖开，05 秒第一层完全立起，07 秒镜头贴近第一层表面。尾帧锁定 @Image2：猫头鹰振翅欲飞，冷蓝背光下剪纸边缘透光。
Clip 2 — 穿过第一层 → 第二层九又四分之三站台（00:08-00:16） 首帧锁定 @Image2。尾帧锁定 @Image3。
00:08-00:12 画面：折纸猫头鹰从第一层枝头起飞，翅膀刚性扇动，拖曳银色纸尘。第一层纸幕如剧场幕布向两侧轻柔卷开/变薄，镜头开始穿透第一层。穿过过程中，第一层纸树与纸云逐渐虚化透明，后方透出暖黄色背光——第二层九又四分之三站台剪纸正在后方亮起。08 秒猫头鹰起飞，10 秒第一层开始分开，11 秒暖光从缝隙中渗出。
00:12-00:16 画面：镜头完全进入第二层景深。哥特式拱廊剪纸层层排列，纸质蒸汽火车头剪影位于中层，暖黄背光从车窗与拱廊后方强烈透出，形成戏剧性皮影戏效果。纸质人影剪影提箱走向火车。前景仍有第一层残留的纸云边缘，增加景深。12 秒火车头显现，14 秒站台全景，15 秒人影登车。尾帧锁定 @Image3：火车头烟囱喷出浓密纸卷烟雾，暖黄背光中烟雾边缘透光。
Clip 3 — 穿过第二层 → 第三层魁地奇球场（00:16-00:24） 首帧锁定 @Image3。尾帧锁定 @Image4。
00:16-00:20 画面：纸卷烟雾弥漫第二层，第二层纸幕如幕布向两侧卷开，镜头穿透烟雾与纸幕。穿过时，暖黄光线逐渐转为炽烈的金色，第三层魁地奇球场剪纸在后方亮起——环形看台层层环绕，追球手剪影骑扫帚悬于中层，金色飞贼为后方强光照亮的镂空纸球。16 秒烟雾中透出金光，18 秒第二层分开，19 秒球场轮廓显现。
00:20-00:24 画面：镜头完全进入第三层。环形看台剪纸层层纵深排列，追球手剪影骑折纸扫帚俯冲，尾翼为镂空纸条，金色飞贼高速旋转。暖金背光从看台后方如舞台聚光灯般透出，形成强烈剪影对比。镜头继续向第三层深处推进，穿过纸质球门环。20 秒球场全景，22 秒追球手俯冲，23 秒穿过球门环。尾帧锁定 @Image4：金色飞贼在画面中心炸开成万千金色纸屑，纸屑在暖光中向镜头飞溅。
Clip 4 — 穿过第三层 → 第四层大礼堂名场面（00:24-00:32） 首帧锁定 @Image4。尾帧锁定 @Image5。
00:24-00:28 画面：金色纸屑如魔术般悬浮，第三层纸幕向两侧卷开，镜头继续纵深推进。纸屑缓缓落下，第四层大礼堂剪纸在后方亮起——长桌纵向排列，纸质烛火以背光透光形式呈现（火焰为镂空剪纸，后方暖琥珀光穿透），天花板悬挂纸星星。镜头穿梭大礼堂，纸尘在体积光束中漂浮。24 秒纸幕分开，26 秒大礼堂亮起，27 秒镜头穿行于长桌之间。
00:28-00:30 画面：大礼堂场景在同一层内快速变换——长桌与烛火剪纸层折叠下沉，厄里斯魔镜剪纸从桌面升起（巴洛克镜框镂空，后方暖光照出模糊人形剪影），随后魔镜折叠消失，魔药课教室剪纸从同一位置升起（纸架子上的烧瓶为彩色透光剪纸）。镜头快速穿梭这三重小景，像翻动画册。28 秒魔镜显现，29 秒魔药课升起。
00:30-00:32 画面：魔药课场景的所有剪纸元素在同一层内逆向展开成平面，碎裂成金白双色纸屑，纸屑被吸入朝向镜头的漩涡。第三层纸幕完全透明化。尾帧锁定 @Image5：纸屑漩涡中心，万千纸屑向心旋转，中心透出微光。
Clip 5 — 穿过第四层 → 第五层禁林守护神（00:32-00:40） 首帧锁定 @Image5。尾帧锁定 @Image6。
00:32-00:36 画面：纸屑漩涡缓缓散开，第四层纸幕向两侧卷开，镜头继续纵深推进。穿过纸屑后，光线转为冷蓝银色——第五层禁林深处剪纸在后方亮起。高大树木剪影层层林立，冷蓝背光从树影后方透出，形成阴森神秘的皮影戏氛围。前景有纸网与纸蜘蛛剪影。32 秒漩涡散开，34 秒第四层分开，35 秒禁林轮廓显现。
00:36-00:40 画面：镜头完全进入第五层。一只折纸牡鹿（守护神）从中层冲出，银白色背光从其纸身内部强烈透出，撞碎前方纸网，纸网碎片在冷光中飘散。牡鹿继续向前冲刺，银白轮廓光在深蓝背景中如月光般耀眼。36 秒牡鹿冲出，38 秒撞碎纸网，39 秒牡鹿跃向镜头。尾帧锁定 @Image6：牡鹿在画面中心碎裂成无数白色纸鹤，纸鹤群振翅向镜头飞来后散开。
Clip 6 — 穿过第五层 → 最深层/回溯闭合（00:40-00:48） 首帧锁定 @Image6。尾帧锁定 @Image1。
00:40-00:43 画面：纸鹤群飞散后，第五层纸幕向两侧卷开，露出最深层——霍格沃茨城堡全景剪纸。这是隧道书最深处、最宏伟的一层：城堡塔楼、禁林、黑湖全部以厚卡纸剪影形式层层排列，最远方是暖金晨光般的强背光，使整个城堡呈现史诗级剪影。镜头在最深层短暂停留，纸鹤从城堡上空飞过。40 秒第五层分开，42 秒最深层城堡全景显现。
00:43-00:48 画面：镜头开始从最深处向后拉（pull-back），一层一层收回纸幕——第五层禁林纸幕从两侧合拢，第四层大礼堂纸幕合拢，第三层魁地奇纸幕合拢，第二层站台纸幕合拢，第一层月夜纸幕合拢。所有纸幕如剧场闭幕般依次收回书本内部。书本竖向缓缓合上，封面与封底合拢。封面 @Image1 烫金标题发出一次暖金色脉冲，然后归于黑暗。48 秒书本完全闭合，与 00:00 首帧不可区分。
强制要求：全片禁止任何文字、字母、数字、符号、字幕。无语音。书本竖立放置，仅在 00:00 竖开一次、00:48 合上一次。总时长 48 秒。统一纸雕灯+隧道书系统：多层厚卡纸剪影平行排列，每层背后独立背光，剪纸边缘透光。场景转换通过"穿过纸幕层"实现，如剧场幕布拉开。镜头纵深推进（push-in）与后退（pull-back），平滑稳定器。外层冷蓝银白，内层暖金琥珀，深层冷蓝转暖金。无平面图形，全部剪纸带厚度、真实阴影、背光轮廓。封面文字仅由 @Image1 提供。
音乐：48 秒连续音轨，无语音干扰。00:00-00:08 清冷钢琴+弦乐，如月夜微风，衬托书本竖开；00:08-00:16 暖光渐入，中提琴+竖琴，随站台亮起；00:16-00:24 炽烈铜管+定音鼓，金色能量随魁地奇推进；00:24-00:30 温暖木管+羽管键琴，巴洛克感随大礼堂蒙太奇；00:30-00:40 恢弘管弦乐全奏，史诗感随禁林航拍与城堡全景；00:40-00:48 减速——大提琴长音+清冷钢琴，纸幕一层层收回，音量渐弱至寂静。音乐重音对齐：03 秒竖开、10 秒穿过第一层、18 秒穿过第二层、26 秒蒙太奇、34 秒穿过第四层、42 秒到达最深层、45 秒开始闭合。
音效：书本竖开吱呀声（厚纸板摩擦）、幕布卷开声（纸张轻柔滑动）、猫头鹰振翅（硬纸板扇动）、火车蒸汽（纸卷释放嘶嘶声）、金色飞贼炸开（纸球爆裂+纸屑飘散）、纸幕层间穿梭（连续纸张摩擦声）、牡鹿冲撞（纸网碎裂）、纸鹤群飞（多层纸板振翅合唱）、书本闭合闷响（厚纸板拍合）。所有音效混音于音乐之下，不可掩盖旋律。
质量：每帧照片级真实感——真实竖立书本、厚卡纸剪纸体积与切割边缘、真实背光透光、可信层叠景深、正确剪影对比。48 秒统一语言——一种纸雕灯系统、一种剧场幕布逻辑、真实竖书物理、五层纵深+闭合循环。无漂移。
（注：封面 @Image1 与五张首尾帧图 @Image2-@Image6 均由 ChatGPT Image-2 生成。六段 8 秒 clip 在 MEDEO 拼接为 48 秒。书本始终竖立。竖开一次，合上一次。首尾帧严格共用。全片无文字无语音。视频由 Grok 生成。）
</user_request>

{"screenplay": "# Harry Potter Paper-Cut Light Box — 48-Second Tunnel Book Film

## Concept
A 48-second cinematic loop built around a vertical tunnel book aesthetic. A real standing book opens once, reveals 5 layers of paper-cut diorama worlds, then closes. Each layer is a Harry Potter scene rendered in thick cardstock silhouettes with independent backlighting — warm gold, cold blue, amber — creating a shadow-box theater of depth and light. Six 8-second clips are stitched seamlessly via shared first/last frames. No text. No voiceover. Pure visual poetry.

## Visual Language
- **Medium**: Paper-cut light box / shadow box / vertical tunnel book
- **Layers**: 5–6 parallel heavy cardstock silhouette planes, 3–5 cm apart
- **Lighting**: Independent backlight behind each layer; warm gold (amber) in inner layers, cold blue/silver in outer layers
- **Edges**: Laser-cut edges glow with backlight halos — visible paper fiber texture, physical cut thickness
- **Subjects**: All figures, animals, buildings rendered as flat cut silhouettes, depth created by layering
- **Transitions**: Each scene change = paper curtain peeling open to both sides like a theater drape, revealing the next layer's backlight glow. No hard cuts. No black. No page turns.
- **Camera**: Continuous dolly-in / push-in through layers; final reversal pull-back through all 5 layers closing the book

## Color Arc
- Outer (Clip 1–2): Cold blue, silver-white, midnight blue — moonlit forest
- Mid (Clip 3–4): Warm gold, amber, candlelight — train platform, Quidditch pitch, Great Hall
- Deep (Clip 5–6): Cold blue → warm gold → dark cover return

## Scenes

### Clip 1 — Book Opening → Forbidden Forest Layer 1 (00:00–00:08)
**First frame**: Closed standing book (@Image1), dark Gothic desk, candlelight rim-lighting the spine.
**00:00–00:03**: Vertical book on dark desk, cover facing forward, atmosphere dim and mysterious. Only ambient light traces the spine.
**00:03–00:08**: Book opens vertically — front and back cover spread apart like a diorama stage opening. First cardstock curtain unfurls from center outward. Moonlit Forbidden Forest emerges: layered paper clouds, paper tree branches, a folded-paper owl perched on a branch. Cold blue backlight illuminates from behind; silver-white glow halos the cloud and branch edges. Camera slowly pushes in toward layer 1 surface.
**Last frame**: Owl poised to take flight, cold blue backlight, paper edges glowing (@Image2).

### Clip 2 — Through Layer 1 → Platform Nine-and-Three-Quarters (00:08–00:16)
**First frame**: @Image2 — Owl on branch, cold blue glow.
**00:08–00:12**: Paper owl launches from branch, rigid paper wings fanning, trailing silver paper dust. First layer paper curtain gently peels open to both sides — paper trees and clouds grow transparent, warm yellow backlight seeps through the parting gap, second layer Nine-and-Three-Quarters platform glowing behind.
**00:12–00:16**: Camera fully enters second layer depth. Gothic arched colonnade silhouettes recede in perspective. Cardstock steam locomotive at mid-layer, warm yellow light pouring from cut-out windows and arches. Human silhouettes with luggage walk toward train. Remnant paper clouds from layer 1 float at foreground edges, reinforcing depth.
**Last frame**: Locomotive chimney billowing dense paper-scroll smoke, warm yellow light halos the smoke edges (@Image3).

### Clip 3 — Through Layer 2 → Quidditch Pitch (00:16–00:24)
**First frame**: @Image3 — Locomotive with paper smoke, warm amber glow.

batch.prompt: A closed vertical hardcover book stands on a dark Gothic desk. For the first 3 seconds it remains still, atmospheric candlelight softly tracing the spine outline, mysterious and silent. Then at 3 seconds the book slowly opens vertically — the front cover and back cover spread apart like a theater stage opening. From the center, the first layer of heavy cardstock paper curtain unfurls outward to both sides, rising up to reveal a moonlit Forbidden Forest paper-cut diorama: layered paper clouds, paper tree branches, and a folded-paper owl perched on a branch. Cold blue backlight activates from behind the paper layers, silver-white glowing halos appear around every cut edge. Camera begins a slow smooth dolly-in push toward the first layer surface, approaching the paper owl. By end the owl is close and ready to take flight, cold blue light blazing.

The paper owl on the branch launches into flight — rigid angular paper wings fan open and begin beating, trailing silver paper dust particles. The first paper layer curtain (paper trees and clouds) gently peels apart from the center, each side rolling softly outward like a theater drape, the paper becoming increasingly transparent. Through the widening gap, warm amber-yellow backlight seeps in from the second layer behind — a Gothic arched colonnade station platform with a cardstock steam locomotive beginning to glow. Camera continues smooth push-in through the parting first layer. In the second half, camera fully enters second layer depth: Gothic arched colonnade silhouettes recede in perspective, cardstock locomotive at center with warm yellow light pouring from cut-out windows, human silhouettes with luggage walking toward the train, remnant paper clouds at foreground edges for depth. Camera advances toward the locomotive. End: locomotive chimney billows dense paper-scroll smoke with warm yellow light halos.

Paper scroll smoke billows and fills the second layer. The second layer paper curtain begins to peel open from the center — each side curling outward softly like a theater drape. Through the parting gap the warm yellow tone transitions to fierce intense gold as the third layer Quidditch pitch emerges: ring-shaped stadium stands in receding parallel cardstock planes, a Seeker figure on a broomstick silhouette diving at center, and a Golden Snitch as a bright cut-out orb. Camera pushes in through the parting second layer. In second half, camera fully inside third layer: ring stands create deep paper perspective, Seeker dives with laser-cut paper strip tail feathers, Golden Snitch spins and rotates rapidly, warm gold backlight from behind stands blazes like stage spotlights creating dramatic silhouette contrast. Camera continues push-in through a paper goal hoop. End: Snitch bursts into an explosion of golden paper fragments and shards flying toward the camera lens.

Golden paper fragments float suspended in warm light, slowly drifting down. The third layer paper curtain peels open from center to both sides. Fourth layer Great Hall glows behind it with warm amber candlelight: long dining tables recede in paper perspective, hollow cut-out candle flames are backlit amber creating glow-through fire effects, paper stars hang from a vaulted ceiling. Camera enters and weaves between the long tables. Then the scene rapidly shifts within the same layer: tables and candles fold down and a baroque mirror frame rises (Mirror of Erised) with warm light casting a vague human silhouette inside it, then the mirror folds away and a Potions classroom rises with jewel-toned translucent flask silhouettes. Then all elements reverse-unfold flat and shatter into gold-white paper fragments. Fragments are pulled into a spiral vortex aimed at camera. Layer becomes transparent, vortex center glows faintly.

The paper vortex slowly disperses and dissolves. The fourth layer paper curtain peels open to both sides, light shifting to cold blue-silver. Fifth layer deep Forbidden Forest emerges: tall tree trunk silhouettes as heavy cardstock planes receding back into depth, cold blue backlight behind each tree layer, eerie shadow-theater atmosphere. Paper web silhouettes and paper spider shapes at foreground. Camera pushes in through the cold forest. Then a folded-paper stag (Patronus) charges out from the mid-layer — silver-white backlight blazes from within its paper body like a paper lantern. The stag crashes through the foreground paper web, web fragments scatter in cold light. Stag continues charging powerfully toward the camera, silver-white glow outline blazing against deep midnight blue. End: stag's paper form fractures into hundreds of small white paper cranes at its edges, the flock launching outward toward camera and dispersing.

White paper cranes scatter and spread apart. The fifth layer paper curtain peels open from center revealing the deepest innermost layer: a grand Hogwarts Castle panorama as massive layered cardstock silhouettes — castle towers, the Forbidden Forest, the Black Lake all as receding parallel paper planes. Farthest back: fierce warm gold morning backlight blazing, casting the entire castle as an epic theatrical silhouette. Camera briefly holds on this magnificent deepest layer view. Paper cranes fly over the castle turrets. Then camera smoothly begins a slow pull-back — moving backward through each layer as the paper curtains draw closed from innermost outward: the fifth layer forest curtain closes from both sides, then fourth layer closes, third closes, second closes, first closes — each like a theater curtain gently drawing shut. Finally the book's front and back covers fold together and the book closes completely vertical. The closed cover emits a single warm gold pulse of light, then fades to darkness matching the opening frame.

[script.md:screenplay] Content (9158 characters, 81 lines):

 1| # Harry Potter Paper-Cut Light Box — 48-Second Tunnel Book Film
 2| 
 3| ## Concept
 4| A 48-second cinematic loop built around a vertical tunnel book aesthetic. A real standing book opens once, reveals 5 layers of paper-cut diorama worlds, then closes. Each layer is a Harry Potter scene rendered in thick cardstock silhouettes with independent backlighting — warm gold, cold blue, amber — creating a shadow-box theater of depth and light. Six 8-second clips are stitched seamlessly via shared first/last frames. No text. No voiceover. Pure visual poetry.
 5| 
 6| ## Visual Language
 7| - **Medium**: Paper-cut light box / shadow box / vertical tunnel book
 8| - **Layers**: 5–6 parallel heavy cardstock silhouette planes, 3–5 cm apart
 9| - **Lighting**: Independent backlight behind each layer; warm gold (amber) in inner layers, cold blue/silver in outer layers
10| - **Edges**: Laser-cut edges glow with backlight halos — visible paper fiber texture, physical cut thickness
11| - **Subjects**: All figures, animals, buildings rendered as flat cut silhouettes, depth created by layering
12| - **Transitions**: Each scene change = paper curtain peeling open to both sides like a theater drape, revealing the next layer's backlight glow. No hard cuts. No black. No page turns.
13| - **Camera**: Continuous dolly-in / push-in through layers; final reversal pull-back through all 5 layers closing the book
14| 
15| ## Color Arc
16| - Outer (Clip 1–2): Cold blue, silver-white, midnight blue — moonlit forest
17| - Mid (Clip 3–4): Warm gold, amber, candlelight — train platform, Quidditch pitch, Great Hall
18| - Deep (Clip 5–6): Cold blue → warm gold → dark cover return
19| 
20| ## Scenes
21| 
22| ### Clip 1 — Book Opening → Forbidden Forest Layer 1 (00:00–00:08)
23| **First frame**: Closed standing book (@Image1), dark Gothic desk, candlelight rim-lighting the spine.
24| **00:00–00:03**: Vertical book on dark desk, cover facing forward, atmosphere dim and mysterious. Only ambient light traces the spine.
25| **00:03–00:08**: Book opens vertically — front and back cover spread apart like a diorama stage opening. First cardstock curtain unfurls from center outward. Moonlit Forbidden Forest emerges: layered paper clouds, paper tree branches, a folded-paper owl perched on a branch. Cold blue backlight illuminates from behind; silver-white glow halos the cloud and branch edges. Camera slowly pushes in toward layer 1 surface.
26| **Last frame**: Owl poised to take flight, cold blue backlight, paper edges glowing (@Image2).
27| 
28| ### Clip 2 — Through Layer 1 → Platform Nine-and-Three-Quarters (00:08–00:16)
29| **First frame**: @Image2 — Owl on branch, cold blue glow.
30| **00:08–00:12**: Paper owl launches from branch, rigid paper wings fanning, trailing silver paper dust. First layer paper curtain gently peels open to both sides — paper trees and clouds grow transparent, warm yellow backlight seeps through the parting gap, second layer Nine-and-Three-Quarters platform glowing behind.
31| **00:12–00:16**: Camera fully enters second layer depth. Gothic arched colonnade silhouettes recede in perspective. Cardstock steam locomotive at mid-layer, warm yellow light pouring from cut-out windows and arches. Human silhouettes with luggage walk toward train. Remnant paper clouds from layer 1 float at foreground edges, reinforcing depth.
32| **Last frame**: Locomotive chimney billowing dense paper-scroll smoke, warm yellow light halos the smoke edges (@Image3).
33| 
34| ### Clip 3 — Through Layer 2 → Quidditch Pitch (00:16–00:24)
35| **First frame**: @Image3 — Locomotive with paper smoke, warm amber glow.
36| **00:16–00:20**: Paper smoke fills layer 2. Second layer curtain peels open. Warm yellow transitions to fierce gold. Quidditch pitch emerges: ring-shaped stands receding in layers, Seeker silhouettes on brooms at mid-layer, Golden Snitch as a glowing cut-out paper orb. Camera pushes in.
37| **00:20–00:24**: Camera fully inside third layer. Ring stands in deep paper perspective. Seeker on paper broom dives, tail feathers rendered as laser-cut paper strips. Golden Snitch spins at high speed. Warm gold backlight from stands acts like stage spotlights. Camera continues push-in through paper goal hoops.
38| **Last frame**: Golden Snitch explodes into thousands of golden paper fragments flying toward lens (@Image4).
39| 
40| ### Clip 4 — Through Layer 3 → Great Hall Montage (00:24–00:32)
41| **First frame**: @Image4 — Gold paper fragments suspended, gold light.
42| **00:24–00:28**: Gold paper fragments float and fall. Third layer curtain peels open. Fourth layer Great Hall glows with warm amber candlelight. Long tables recede in paper perspective; cut-out candle flames backlit amber through hollow silhouettes; paper stars hang from vaulted ceiling. Camera weaves between long tables.
43| **00:28–00:30**: Within same layer, scene shifts rapidly — long tables and candles fold down; Mirror of Erised rises (baroque mirror frame cut-out, warm light casting vague human silhouette within mirror); mirror folds away; Potions classroom rises (glass flasks as colored translucent cut-out paper, backlit in jewel tones).
44| **00:30–00:32**: All Potions elements reverse-unfold to flat plane, shatter into gold-and-white paper fragments, fragments sucked into a vortex pointing toward camera. Layer becomes transparent.
45| **Last frame**: Vortex of paper fragments at center, spiraling inward, faint light at vortex core (@Image5).
46| 
47| ### Clip 5 — Through Layer 4 → Forbidden Forest Patronus (00:32–00:40)
48| **First frame**: @Image5 — Paper fragment vortex, cold light returning.
49| **00:32–00:36**: Vortex of fragments disperses. Fourth layer curtain peels open. Light shifts to cold blue-silver. Fifth layer deep Forbidden Forest glows: tall tree silhouettes recede in layers, cold blue backlight behind each trunk, eerie shadow-theater atmosphere. Paper web and paper spider silhouettes at foreground.
50| **00:36–00:40**: A folded-paper stag (Patronus) charges from mid-layer, silver-white backlight blazing from within its paper body. It crashes through foreground paper web; web fragments scatter in cold light. Stag continues charging toward camera, silver-white outline blazing like moonlight against deep blue.
51| **Last frame**: Stag shatters into hundreds of white paper cranes, flock launching toward camera then dispersing (@Image6).
52| 
53| ### Clip 6 — Through Layer 5 → Hogwarts + All Layers Close (00:40–00:48)
54| **First frame**: @Image6 — Paper cranes dispersing, cold blue turning warm.
55| **00:40–00:43**: Paper cranes scatter. Fifth layer curtain peels open, revealing the deepest layer: Hogwarts Castle panorama. Castle towers, Forbidden Forest, Black Lake all rendered as massive layered cardstock silhouettes. Farthest back: fierce warm gold morning-light backlight, casting the entire castle as an epic silhouette. Camera lingers. Paper cranes fly over castle turrets.
56| **00:43–00:48**: Camera reverses — slow pull-back. Layer by layer, paper curtains close from innermost out: Layer 5 (Forbidden Forest) draws shut from both sides, Layer 4 (Great Hall) draws shut, Layer 3 (Quidditch) draws shut, Layer 2 (Platform) draws shut, Layer 1 (Forest) draws shut — each like a theater curtain closing. Book closes vertically, front and back covers fold together. Cover (@Image1) emits one warm gold pulse from gilded title, then fades to darkness. Final frame is identical to 00:00 opening frame — perfect loop.
57| 
58| ## Music
59| 48-second continuous orchestral score, no voice interference.
60| - **00:00–00:08**: Clear piano + strings, moonlit breeze, underscores book opening
61| - **00:08–00:16**: Warm light enters — viola + harp, rises with platform glow
62| - **00:16–00:24**: Fierce brass + timpani, golden energy with Quidditch push
63| - **00:24–00:30**: Warm woodwind + harpsichord, baroque warmth through Great Hall montage
64| - **00:30–00:40**: Full orchestra, epic sweep through forest and castle
65| - **00:40–00:48**: Decelerates — cello sustain + clear piano, paper curtains close one by one, volume fades to silence
66| 
67| **Music accent hits**: 3s (book opens), 10s (pass layer 1), 18s (pass layer 2), 26s (montage), 34s (pass layer 4), 42s (deepest layer), 45s (close begins)
68| 
69| ## Sound Design
70| Book opening creak (thick cardboard friction), curtain peel (soft paper slide), owl wings (rigid paper fan), train steam (paper roll hiss), Snitch burst (paper ball pop + fragment flutter), layer transitions (continuous paper friction), stag charge (paper web shatter), paper crane flock (multi-layer cardboard wing chorus), book close (thick cardboard thud). All SFX mixed beneath music, never masking melody.
71| 
72| ## Technical Requirements
73| - No text, letters, numbers, symbols, or subtitles anywhere in the video
74| - No voiceover
75| - Book stands vertical throughout; opens once at 00:00, closes once at 00:48
76| - All 6 clips connected via shared first/last frames (Clip N last = Clip N+1 first)
77| - Clip 1 first frame and Clip 6 last frame = @Image1 (perfect loop)
78| - Paper-cut light box aesthetic throughout: multi-layer cardstock silhouettes, independent backlighting per layer, physical paper texture and cut-edge depth
79| - Scene transitions via "paper curtain parting" — never hard cuts, never black screen
80| - Photorealistic paper craft quality: real cardstock volume, real backlight glow, real cast shadows, believable layered depth
81|

# Knowledge: Seedance 2.0 Full Production Guide

## Character Consistency

Character identity routing — which reference field to use (images / videos / platform virtual avatars), reuse rules, and reject checks — lives in the `consistency/character-multi-ref` fragment. Load it for any character-consistent Seedance production; it is the single source of truth for identity handling. Seedance-specific reference prep and the hard virtual-avatar rule below still apply.

Fixed-cast stories are character-consistent even when the user does not say "keep them consistent": sports teams, competitions, families, bands, partners, classmates, girl/boy groups, or "N people" who carry the action need character references. Do not write that such people are "only a crowd", "style consistency is enough", or "individual precision is unnecessary" unless they are clearly one-off background extras. For counted fixed casts up to 9 people, list numbered member slots (for example Athlete 1-8) and prepare one reference per member slot; team/crowd collage references are not a substitute for member identity.

**Reference Image Preparation** (critical — do NOT generate separate T2I images for each angle, they will be inconsistent):
1. **Single multi-angle sheet** (preferred): Use `generate_text_to_image` to generate ONE image containing the character from multiple angles (front, side, 3/4 view) in a single picture
2. **I2I derivation**: Generate one initial reference with T2I → use `generate_images_to_image` to derive additional angle variants from that single reference

**⚠️ Platform Virtual Avatars (hard rule — characters marked "Virtual avatar" in their info)**:
- When a referenced character is marked as a virtual avatar (you will see "Virtual avatar" or
  "Also registered as a virtual avatar" in the character info injected with the user message),
  you MUST use `reference_character_ids` with the character's ID — do NOT extract its ref images
  and put them in `reference_image_media_ids`. The harness resolves character IDs to registered
  asset IDs that bypass Seedance's content policy filters. Passing raw ref images directly will
  trigger real-person detection and fail.
- This only applies to `generate_multi_ref_to_video`. For other tools (T2I, I2I, I2V with non-Seedance models) that don't
  support `reference_character_ids`, use the character's ref image IDs normally.

## Scene Consistency

For coherent stories, scene/environment consistency across shots is almost always needed — the same approach as character consistency, but for backgrounds.

**Reference Image Preparation**:
1. **Generate a scene reference**: Use `generate_text_to_image` to create a reference image of the environment/location (e.g. a coffee shop interior, a rainy alley, a spaceship bridge)
2. **Multiple angles** (optional): Generate a single image containing 2–3 views of the same location (wide establishing shot + detail close-up) for stronger environment consistency — same approach as character multi-angle sheets

**Using Scene References**:
- Label scene references with `Scene:` at the top of the prompt (e.g. `Scene: image_6, image_7`)
- The model uses these to maintain consistent background, lighting, and spatial layout across shots
- For multi-shot stories: generate scene references once, reuse across all calls that share the same location
- If the story spans multiple locations, prepare separate scene references for each location
- If the user already uploaded scene/reference images, map each original uploaded media ID to a concrete room/location before planning any shots
- In the final `generate_multi_ref_to_video` call, keep the matching original uploaded media ID in `reference_image_media_ids`; derived images can be added as extra refs, but must not replace the original uploaded image

## Style Consistency (Optional)

When a unified visual style is needed across shots (e.g. a specific art style or color palette), generate a style reference image with `generate_text_to_image`, include it in `reference_image_media_ids`, and label it with `Style:` at the top of the prompt. Describe the style once in the prompt body to reinforce it. Combine with `style_postfix` for best results.

## Audio

- **Audio is always on**: Every Seedance video includes synchronized audio (dialogue, SFX, ambient) by default — there is no separate flag to enable it
- **Use native audio for ALL speech in Seedance workflows (MANDATORY)**: Seedance 2.0 has exceptionally strong native audio — it generates speech with emotion, tone, lip-sync, natural pauses, and breathing. When using the Seedance workflow, you MUST use native audio for ALL speech (dialogue, narration, presentation, voiceover, etc.) instead of TTS. Write speech directly in the video prompt using `says:` syntax. Do NOT use TTS (`generate_text_to_speech`) for Seedance workflows. The ONLY exception is when the user literally says "use TTS" or "use text-to-speech" by name. This rule applies to ALL video types including science explainers, documentaries, tutorials, brand ads, short dramas, and narrated content — write narration as narrator character speech using `says:` syntax
- **"旁白配音" means native narration, NOT TTS**: When a user says "需要旁白配音" or "需要配音", they want spoken narration in the video — they are NOT requesting TTS technology. Implement narration by writing it as a narrator voice in the video prompt using `says:` syntax. For example: `A warm male narrator voice says: "[narration in the task's language]"`. Seedance will generate this narration natively with natural emotion and timing. This IS the "配音" the user wants
- **Why native audio over TTS for Seedance**: Seedance is one of the few models whose native audio quality exceeds TTS — it provides lip-sync, emotional delivery, and natural vocal performance. TTS produces robotic, stiff narration that degrades the quality of story-driven, brand, and emotional content. TTS is only acceptable for pure science/news/tutorial content where a clinical tone is appropriate
- **If TTS is used** (e.g., user explicitly says "use TTS"): generate TTS first, then plan shot timing around the narration duration. Specify "no human speech" in the video prompt so native audio only produces ambient/SFX. **Ensure TTS is not added to shots where the prompt specifies "no human speech" — this constraint must be respected in the final timeline assembly**
- **BGM (Background Music)**: Seedance native audio generates ambient sounds and SFX but does not produce a full background music track. For videos that need BGM, search for a suitable track using `asset_search_bgm`, or generate one with `generate_text_to_music`, then add it to the music track on the timeline
- **Spoken language matching**: All dialogue, narration, voiceover, and spoken content in the video prompt must use the user's explicitly requested spoken language. If no spoken language is specified, use the primary language of the user's task description. Do not translate spoken content into another language unless the user explicitly asks. When the user emphasizes a spoken language preference, include an explicit instruction in the video prompt (e.g. `Spoken language: all dialogue and narration are in English.`)

## Script Writing Conventions

The director_note must contain **complete, ready-to-use prompts** — not outlines or summaries. Default to **medium-to-long narrative complexity**: describe the environment, character micro-actions, emotional beats, and sensory details (see Example 4 below). Only use one-liner prompts for trivially simple scenes (e.g. a single product shot or a quick concept test).

**⚠️ Duration Planning (CRITICAL for videos ≥ 2 minutes)**:
- Seedance 2.0 max clip duration: **15 seconds**
- For a 2-minute video: `ceil(120s / 15s) = 8 clips minimum`
- For a 3-minute video: `ceil(180s / 15s) = 12 clips minimum`
- **Common mistake**: Planning only 4-5 shots for a 2-minute video — this yields ~60-75s max, far below target
- Always calculate: `min_clips = ceil(target_duration / 15)` and ensure your shot list meets this count

When writing the director_note for a Seedance workflow:
- **Reference plan**: List characters/subjects (1 multi-angle sheet per character, or an explicit grouped reference plan for large fixed casts), scenes/locations (1–2 reference images per location), and optionally a style reference. For fixed casts that fit Seedance's image-reference budget (up to 9 people), use one numbered member slot/reference per person instead of crowd or team-collage references, and write the numeric coverage in the plan (for example: "8 athlete references: Athlete 1 ... Athlete 8").
- **Global roster binding**: For fixed casts, write one global `Role → Figure slot → reference variable` map and keep it stable across every clip. Do not reuse a global Figure number for a different character in a later prompt.
- **Prompt drafts**: Write full narrative prompts using the five-element structure (Subject → Action → Camera → Style → Constraints) — include environment atmosphere, character body language, micro-expressions, and audio cues
- **Per-clip reference coverage**: Before each video prompt draft, list which global roster slots appear in the clip and ensure each one has a matching reference in that task. If a named/slotted character appears in the prompt, its reference must be passed to the same `generate_multi_ref_to_video` task.
- **Figure notation**: Use "Figure 1", "Figure 2" to reference characters (never real names). For fixed casts, these are global character slots; if the tool call passes only a subset of references, label the local image with the global slot (for example, `Figure 6 (Rival): image_2`) instead of using only local `image_N` labels or renumbering the character as a different global Figure.
- **Timeline markers**: For multi-shot videos (>5s), use `[00-05s]` markers
- **Audio notes**: Describe desired dialogue/SFX per shot in the prompt
- **Action causality**: For sports, battles, chases, dances, competitions, escapes, or any action-driven story, verify that each clip's result explains the next clip's starting state. If a ball, vehicle, weapon, pursued person, lead performer, or other key object changes position/owner, include the handoff, rebound, block, dodge, pursuit, or reaction that makes the transition believable.

## Workflow
1. Generate ONE multi-angle reference sheet per character/subject (front + side + 3/4 view in a single image)
   - For a counted fixed cast of up to 9 people, each person is a separate character/subject. Generate one reference sheet per member slot (for example Athlete 1, Athlete 2, ... Athlete 8); do not generate a single team, crowd, or group portrait as the identity reference.
2. For coherent stories: generate scene/environment reference images for each location
3. Optionally: generate a style reference image if a specific visual style is needed across shots
4. Optionally add a reference video (motion style) or audio (audio style/mood reference)
5. Write a prompt following the Seedance 2.0 methodology below
6. Call `generate_multi_ref_to_video` with reference media IDs, the prompt, and a `style_postfix` for unified style
   (Mandatory — do not skip this call based on assumptions about service availability. See the Mandatory Execution Attempt rule in the workflow prompt.)
7. When uploaded images are available, the final video call must still include those original uploaded image IDs for the corresponding subject/scene

For fixed-cast character stories, a zero-reference multi-ref call is not a character-consistency route. If identity matters, first obtain character reference media, then pass them through `reference_image_media_ids`, `reference_video_media_ids`, or `reference_character_ids` as appropriate.

If the director_note says references will be generated, those image/reference tasks must be called and waited before the character video call. Do not write a reference plan and then execute the same character shots as "T2V (0 references)".

---

## Seedance 2.0 Prompt Methodology

### Core Principle: Write Intent, Not Details

Seedance 2.0 has built-in director thinking and world knowledge. Do NOT pile up adjectives or micro-manage every frame. The model automatically arranges shots and fills in reasonable details.

Key rules:
1. **Focus on motion** — describe what moves, how fast, and where; skip static appearance when references already define it
2. **Negative prompts don't work** — never write "don't include X"; describe what you want instead
3. **Use specific camera terms** — "slow dolly-in, eye level" works; "dynamic cinematic" is meaningless
4. **Degree adverbs matter** — "swiftly runs" vs "runs" produce very different motion amplitude
5. **One style anchor > many adjectives** — "Wes Anderson palette" beats "pastel, symmetrical, whimsical"

### Five-Element Structure

Follow this order for best results (each element is optional but order matters):

Subject → Action → Camera → Style → (Constraints)

- **Subject** first: locks model attention (use "Figure 1" / "Figure 2" to reference uploaded characters)
- **Action** second: the dynamic anchor — verbs + motion degree
- **Camera** third: shot size + movement + angle (prevents random angle switching)
- **Style** fourth: one visual anchor (film stock, director name, or art movement)
- **Constraints** (optional): guardrails for lighting, color, duration, audio cues — often unnecessary

### Reference Labeling in Prompts

When using multiple reference images for different roles (characters, scenes, props), label them at the top of the prompt so the model knows which image maps to which role:

Figure 1: image_1, image_2, image_3
Figure 2: image_4, image_5
Scene: image_6, image_7

Each label can map to one or more images. Multiple images per label (e.g. different angles of the same character) strengthen identity consistency. Then write the rest of the prompt below. "Figure N" labels character/subject references; "Scene" labels background/environment references. This keeps identity assignment unambiguous when multiple references are passed.

For fixed casts across multiple clips, keep a global roster map outside the local `image_N` array. The `image_N` labels are local to the current tool call; the character alias is global. If Figure 6 is the Rival, every prompt involving that character should label the local reference as `Figure 6 (Rival): image_N`, even when it is local `image_2` in a two-reference clip.

### Multi-Shot (Recommended)

Seedance 2.0 has extremely strong instruction-following for multi-shot. Two approaches:

**Approach 1 — Script-first (preferred, simpler)**:
Write the story directly, then append a multi-shot suffix to let the model design camera work autonomously:

[Story / narrative description here]
Multi-shot, fast cuts, varied shot sizes, includes close-ups and wide shots

The suffix tells the model the desired shot frequency, framing variety, etc. You write the **what** (story); the model decides the **how** (camera angles, cuts, transitions).

**Approach 2 — Full control (detailed)**:
Use **timeline markers** when you want precise control over every shot:

[00-05s] Shot description with specific camera...
[05-10s] Shot description with specific camera...
[10-15s] Shot description with specific camera...

If you specify shots in detail, Seedance follows your design exactly.

**Key difference from Sora / Kling**: Seedance's instruction-following is strong enough that both approaches work reliably — other models may need more explicit shot descriptions to produce good results.

### Duration and Pacing Planning

**Core principle: generate as much story as possible in a single call.** A story that fits in 12s should not be split into two calls — segments generated separately are difficult to keep consistent in voice and style. **Let content determine duration, not the other way around.**

| Content type | Suggested duration |
|-------------|--------------------|
| Single action / product showcase | 4–6s |
| Short emotional scene (no dialogue) | 6–10s |
| Dialogue scene (2–4 lines) | 10–13s |
| Complete short story (multi-character + turn) | 12–15s |

Allow at least 2–3s per dialogue line; when using timeline markers (`[00-05s]`), align them to actual dialogue volume — do not compress 3 lines of dialogue into 4s.

Pacing suffix reference:
- Fast action: `Multi-shot, fast cuts, handheld urgency, wide-to-closeup progression`
- Drama / dialogue: `Multi-shot, medium pacing, shot-reverse-shot during dialogue, close-ups on faces`
- Slow atmosphere: `Single long take` or `Multi-shot, slow pacing, minimal cuts`

### Prompt Examples

Example 1 — One-liner T2V (no references, simplest form)

A golden retriever puppy chases a butterfly across a sunlit meadow, stumbles, rolls over, then bounces back up wagging its tail. Handheld, wide to close-up.

Reference setup: none (pure T2V).

Example 2 — Product showcase (five-element style, compact)

Figure 1: image_1, image_2, image_3

Figure 1 (a minimalist glass perfume bottle). Placed on a white marble surface, water droplets form on the cool glass exterior and slowly trickle down.
Extreme close-up, slow dolly-in, high angle, macro lens.
Studio fashion photography, cool tungsten backlight + soft fill from left, shallow depth of field, muted silver tones.
No text, no hands, no sudden cuts.

Reference setup: 3 product photos (front, side, top).

Example 3 — Script-first multi-shot (no dialogue, model designs camera)

Figure 1: image_1

Figure 1 sprints down the steps of a train station, weaving through commuters. Spots someone waving from the platform — face breaks into a wide grin. Accelerates. The train doors begin to close. Last second, she dives through, collapsing against the doors, breathless, laughing.

Multi-shot, fast cuts, framing progresses from wide establishing to extreme close-up, handheld urgency throughout.

Audio: station ambience, rushing footsteps, crowd murmur, train door chime, relieved exhale.

Reference setup: 1 multi-angle sheet of the character.

Example 4 — Rich narrative multi-shot + dialogue (novelistic detail, model designs camera)

Figure 1: image_1, image_2
Figure 2: image_3, image_4
Scene: image_5

Style: contemporary drama, warm afternoon light filtered through dusty blinds, slice-of-life realism with a Wong Kar-wai melancholy.

The café is almost empty. Afternoon light slants through half-closed venetian blinds, casting striped shadows across the table. A half-finished latte sits untouched, foam long collapsed.

Figure 1 sits alone by the window, one hand wrapped around the cold cup, the other tracing idle circles on the condensation ring it left on the wooden table. Her gaze drifts past the glass — not watching anything, just somewhere far away. A strand of hair falls across her cheek; she doesn't bother to push it back.

The door chime rings. Figure 2 steps in, pauses at the threshold, scanning the room. He spots Figure 1 and something tightens in his jaw — a flicker of hesitation before he walks over, pulling out the chair across from her. The chair leg scrapes against the tile floor.

He sits. A beat of silence. Figure 2 leans forward slightly, elbows on the table, and says in a calm, slightly husky male voice: "You didn't reply to my message."

Figure 1's fingers stop tracing. She looks up — slowly, as if the motion costs her something — meets his eyes for a fraction of a second, then drops her gaze back to the cup. In a quiet, slightly raspy female voice: "I know."

The silence stretches. Somewhere behind the counter, a spoon clinks against ceramic. Figure 2 studies her face, searching. He leans closer.

Figure 2 says softly: "Are you okay?"

Figure 1's composure cracks — just barely. The corner of her mouth twitches upward into a small, sad smile that doesn't reach her eyes. She exhales, almost a laugh, almost a sigh: "I will be."

Multi-shot, medium pacing, intimate framing, close-ups on faces during dialogue, slow push-ins during silences.

Figure 1: image_1, image_2
Figure 2: image_3
Scene: image_4

Style: urban thriller, overcast daylight, desaturated tones, handheld urgency.

[00-03s] Close-up on Figure 1, back against a brick wall, breathing fast.
Figure 1 says in a low, urgent whisper: "Did anyone follow you?"

[03-06s] Wide shot. Figure 2 steps into the alley, looks both ways.
Figure 2 replies in a flat, controlled voice: "No. We have maybe five minutes."

[06-10s] Two-shot, tight framing. Figure 1 hands an envelope to Figure 2.
Figure 1: "Don't open it until you're out of the city."
Figure 2 takes it without looking down, eyes still on Figure 1.

[10-13s] Extreme close-up on Figure 2's eyes. A brief nod.
Figure 2, barely audible: "I'll find you."

Audio: distant city traffic, wind through the alley, no score, raw voice performances.

### Prompt Tips
- Use **"Figure 1", "Figure 2"** to refer to subjects from uploaded references — avoids copyright filters (never use real character names)
- When references already show the subject clearly, do NOT repeat appearance details — just describe motion and scene
- For I2V (single reference image as first frame): describe only the **change** — motion, camera movement, audio — not what's already visible
- Add degree adverbs to all motion: "gently", "swiftly", "dramatically" — the model cannot guess amplitude from images alone
- Use specific camera terms (dolly-in, pan left, crane up, handheld) instead of vague words (dynamic, cinematic, beautiful)
- For multi-shot videos (>5s), prefer the script-first approach with a multi-shot suffix; use timeline markers `[00-05s]` only when precise shot control is needed
- **Writing dialogue**: embed lines into the narrative using `says:`, e.g. `Figure 1 says: "line here"`; describe the voice on first appearance (e.g. `in a warm, slightly nervous female voice`) and restate it in the `Audio:` section to keep voice consistent across shots

batch.prompt: A vertical hardcover book with gold lettering stands closed on a dark Gothic wooden desk. The right fore-edge of the cover lifts and swings leftward on its spine hinge, opening the book right-to-left like a real hardcover. As the cover swings open, the interior reveals its first layer: a paper-cut diorama of a moonlit Forbidden Forest. Thick cardstock silhouette planes — layered paper clouds, bare tree branches — rise and unfurl from the book's center outward like a theater stage assembling. A folded-paper white owl perches on a center branch. Cold icy blue backlight ignites from behind all paper layers, silver-white glowing halos tracing every laser-cut edge. Camera begins a slow smooth dolly-in from outside the book, pushing gently toward the first paper layer surface. Motion is slow, deliberate, cinematic.

The folded-paper white owl on the branch stirs, spreads its angular paper wings, and launches into flight — rigid paper feathers fanning, trailing silver paper dust. The first cardstock paper curtain (paper trees and clouds) gently peels apart from the center, each side curling outward like a theater drape. The paper becomes increasingly transparent as it parts. Through the widening gap, warm amber-yellow backlight seeps in from behind — the second layer illuminates: Gothic arched colonnade silhouettes receding in layers, a large cardstock steam locomotive at center glowing with warm yellow light from cut-out windows, human silhouettes with luggage walking toward it. Remnant paper clouds at foreground edges add depth. Camera continues a smooth dolly-in through the parting first curtain and into the second layer. Motion is fluid and continuous, no cuts.

Paper-scroll smoke from the locomotive chimney fills the second layer, billowing outward. The second cardstock paper curtain peels open from the center — each side curls away softly like a theater drape. Warm yellow tones transition to fierce intense gold as the third layer emerges: a Quidditch stadium with ring-shaped stands as receding parallel cardstock silhouette planes. A Seeker figure on a broomstick dives at center, laser-cut paper strip tail feathers trailing. A Golden Snitch — a hollow glowing cut-out orb — spins and pulses at the center, then bursts outward into thousands of gold paper fragments and shards flying toward the camera lens. Warm gold backlight from behind the stadium stands blazes like stage spotlights. Camera pushes in smoothly through the parting curtain and deep into the stadium layer.

Gold paper fragments float suspended in warm light, slowly drifting and falling. The third cardstock paper curtain peels open to reveal the fourth layer: the Great Hall rendered in warm amber candlelight — long tables recede in paper perspective, hollow cut-out candle flames glow amber through their silhouettes, paper stars hang from a vaulted ceiling. Camera weaves between the long tables. Then the Great Hall elements fold flat and compress: a baroque Mirror of Erised rises as an intricate cardstock cut-out frame, warm light casting a vague human silhouette inside its hollow opening. Then a Potions classroom rises with jewel-toned translucent flask shapes backlit in rich color. All paper elements then reverse-unfold, shatter into micro-cut paper confetti in gold and white, fragments spiraling inward into a clockwise vortex aimed at the camera. All paper fiber texture and laser-cut edge thickness remain photorealistic throughout. No cartoon lines.

The paper vortex at center slowly dissolves and disperses outward. The fourth cardstock paper curtain peels apart from the center, light shifting from warm amber to cold blue-silver. The fifth layer deep Forbidden Forest emerges: tall tree trunk silhouettes as heavy cardstock planes receding in depth, cold blue backlight behind each tree layer, eerie shadow-theater atmosphere. Paper web silhouettes and paper spider shapes at foreground. Camera pushes through the cold forest. A folded-paper stag (Patronus) emerges from the mid-layer, silver-white backlight blazing from within its paper body like a paper lantern. It charges forward powerfully, crashing through the foreground paper web — web fragments scatter in cold light. The stag's paper form fractures at its edges into dozens of small white paper cranes, the flock launching outward toward the camera and dispersing across the frame.

White paper cranes scatter and spread apart in cold blue light. The fifth cardstock paper curtain peels open revealing the deepest innermost layer: Hogwarts Castle as massive layered cardstock silhouettes — castle towers, Forbidden Forest, Black Lake all as receding parallel paper planes. Fierce warm gold morning backlight blazes from the farthest back, casting the entire castle as an epic theatrical silhouette. Paper cranes fly over castle turrets. Then camera smoothly begins a slow pull-back — moving backward as all paper curtains draw closed from innermost outward: fifth layer forest curtain closes from both sides, then fourth layer closes, third, second, first — each like a theater curtain gently drawing shut in sequence. The book's front and back covers fold together and the book closes vertically. The closed cover emits one warm gold light pulse from its gilded title, then fades to darkness — matching the opening frame of a closed book on a dark Gothic desk.

<user_request>
C2V是什么
</user_request>

C2V 是 **CSS-to-Video** 的简称——您在请求里粘贴了 CSS 动画代码，意思是希望按照这份 CSS 定义的动画效果（圆环展开、图例滑入、数字淡入等）生成对应的视频。

实现方式是把 CSS 动画逻辑翻译成视频生成提示词，然后用 T2V（文字生视频）或 I2V（图片生视频）来实现，并不是一个独立的技术术语或工具——是您这个需求场景下的说法。

# 立体书安利片 — 完整制作提示词模板

## 【第一步：项目定义】

```
制作一部 [总时长]秒 的电影感立体书安利片。
目标书籍：《[书名]》
视觉系统：纸雕灯 / 竖向隧道书（Paper-Cut Light Box / Vertical Tunnel Book）
核心规则：全片无可读文字（封面书名除外）、无字幕、无语音旁白（TTS独立配音）
结构：[N]段 × [每段秒数]秒视频 + 结尾数据总结页
```

---

## 【第二步：封面图生成】（GPT Image-2）

```
生成竖立实体书封面图，16:9横幅。
书名：《[书名]》，[书名原文/译文]
封面材质：[皮革/布面/纸板]，颜色：[主色]
装饰风格：[哥特巴洛克/极简/复古/东方]，烫金/压纹细节
书本竖立闭合，置于[深色桌面/木桌/大理石台]，背景[暗黑/渐变]
仅封面有[烛光/台灯/侧光]反射，无其他文字
风格：photorealistic book cover photography, real physical leather hardcover, 
studio candlelit lighting, ultra sharp, deep shadows
```

---

## 【第三步：各层首尾帧关键帧图】（GPT Image-2，共N+1张）

**每张图的通用模板：**
```
Vertical tunnel book paper-cut light box diorama, [第N层] layer.
场景内容：[书中对应场景，如：主角的家、故事发生地、高潮场景]
前景：[纸质元素1]、[纸质元素2]作为厚卡纸剪影
中层：[标志性物件/人物]剪影
背光：[冷蓝/暖金/琥珀]色背光从纸层后方透出，切割边缘发光
Real cardstock fiber texture, laser-cut edge thickness, 
photorealistic paper craft photography. No text no letters no symbols.
```

**色调规划（可自定义）：**
- 外层（前1-2段）：冷色调（冷蓝/银白/月光）
- 中层（中间段）：暖色调（暖金/琥珀/烛光）
- 深层（后段）：戏剧性对比（冷转暖 或 暖转冷）
- 收尾：回归封面基调

## 【第四步：视频生成】（Seedance 2.0，FL2V首尾帧锁定）

**每段 clip 的通用提示词结构：**

```
[Clip N — 场景描述]
首帧锁定：[对应关键帧图]
尾帧锁定：[对应下一张关键帧图]

[场景动作描述]：
- 前N秒：[当前层内容的动态展现]
- 后N秒：[纸幕从中央向两侧卷开，露出下一层背光]
- 相机：慢速纵深推进（slow dolly-in），平稳无抖动

转场规则（每段通用）：
The cardstock paper curtain peels apart from the center, 
each side curling outward softly like a theater drape. 
Through the widening gap, [下一层色温] backlight seeps in.
Camera continues smooth push-in through the parting curtain.
No hard cuts, no black frames, no page turns.

收尾段（最后一clip）额外加：
Camera smoothly reverses into a slow pull-back, 
all paper curtains close layer by layer from innermost outward,
book covers fold together vertically, 
cover emits one warm gold light pulse, fades to darkness.

全局风格约束（每段都加）：
Heavy cardstock silhouettes, real paper fiber texture, 
laser-cut edge thickness 3-4mm, independent backlight per layer,
glowing halos on cut edges, real cast shadows between layers,
photorealistic paper craft, no cartoon style, no flat illustration.
```

---

## 【第五步：TTS 配音】（British Warwick 音色）

**台词设计原则：**
```
- 每段台词时长 ≤ 对应clip时长 × 80%
- 从clip开始后约200-500ms放置
- 风格：极简、悬念感、电影感，每句不超过10个英文单词
- 每句对应一个画面事件，而非描述画面

模板（6段结构）：
Clip1（封面开启）："[一句引入悬念的话，暗示书的核心主题]"
Clip2（第一层场景）："[书中第一个标志性元素] [简短动作/状态]."
Clip3（第二层场景）："[核心冲突/高潮元素]. [情绪词]."  
Clip4（第三层场景）："[书中最温暖/最重要的场景]. [一个感受词]."
Clip5（第四层场景）："[书中最震撼的意象]. [节奏感强的3个短句]."
Clip6（收尾））："Every time you open this book — [书给读者的核心价值]."
```

---

## 【第六步：结尾数据总结页】（Seedance T2V，8-10秒）

```
生成纸雕灯风格同心圆环数据动画视频，近黑色背景。
标题：《[书名]》 By The Numbers
5个圆环数据（填入真实数据）：
- 圆环1（最外）：[数据1，如全球销量] [百分比]%
- 圆环2：[数据2，如译本语言数] [百分比]%  
- 圆环3：[数据3，如改编作品票房] [百分比]%
- 圆环4：[数据4，如读者评分/奖项] [百分比]%
- 圆环5（最内）：[数据5，如复读率/出版年限] [百分比]%
中心：[最核心数字，如"500M+"]

动画逻辑：圆环从外到内依次顺时针展开亮起 → 
右侧图例逐条从右滑入 → 中心数字最后亮起
材质：全程厚卡纸弧形剪影、激光切割边缘透光、烛光侧打

TTS台词模板："[数据1]. [数据2]. [数据3]. 
One story — [书的核心价值/召唤行动]."
```

## 【第七步：时间线组装规则】

```
组装顺序：视频clips → speeches → BGM
clips：依次首尾相连，无黑场
speeches：每段从对应clip开始后200-500ms放置，

     时长：自动延伸到主轨结尾
```

content_parts.text:
模型：Grok Video Generation，6 段 × 8 秒，MEDEO 拼接为 48 秒。
核心原则：全片禁止任何可读文字、字母、数字、符号、字幕。无语音旁白。书本仅在 00:00 竖向打开一次，在 00:48 竖向合上一次。中间所有场景通过"穿过纸幕层"实现转换，禁止翻页、禁止黑场。六段首尾帧严格共用：clip1 尾帧 = clip2 首帧，clip2 尾帧 = clip3 首帧，clip3 尾帧 = clip4 首帧，clip4 尾帧 = clip5 首帧，clip5 尾帧 = clip6 首帧。clip1 首帧与 clip6 尾帧共用 @Image1，形成完美循环。
视觉风格 — Paper-Cut Light Box / Shadow Box： 全片采用纸雕灯与竖向隧道书（vertical tunnel book）美学。书本竖立放置于深色桌面上，打开后内部是 5-6 层平行排列的厚卡纸剪影（heavy cardstock silhouettes），每层如同剧场幕布，彼此间隔 3-5 厘米，形成强烈景深。每层卡纸背后有独立背光源（backlight），使剪纸边缘透出暖金或冷蓝轮廓光（glowing halos around cut edges），正面则呈现深影剪影。人物、动物、建筑均为平面剪纸，但多层叠加后产生立体纵深感。卡纸表面可见真实纤维纹理与激光切割边缘厚度。
色调：外层（clip1-2）冷蓝月夜、银白、午夜蓝；内层（clip3-4）暖金琥珀、烛光色；深层（clip5-6）冷蓝转暖金，最终回归封面暗调。
镜头：纵深推进（dolly-in / push-in），从书外逐层向最深处穿透。穿过某层纸幕时，该层如剧场幕布向两侧轻柔卷开/分开/变薄，露出后一层背光轮廓，不可生硬切换。

# Harry Potter Paper-Cut Light Box — 48-Second Tunnel Book Film

## Concept
A 48-second cinematic loop built around a vertical tunnel book aesthetic. A real standing book opens once, reveals 5 layers of paper-cut diorama worlds, then closes. Each layer is a Harry Potter scene rendered in thick cardstock silhouettes with independent backlighting — warm gold, cold blue, amber — creating a shadow-box theater of depth and light. Six 8-second clips are stitched seamlessly via shared first/last frames. No text. No voiceover. Pure visual poetry.

## Visual Language
- **Medium**: Paper-cut light box / shadow box / vertical tunnel book
- **Layers**: 5–6 parallel heavy cardstock silhouette planes, 3–5 cm apart
- **Lighting**: Independent backlight behind each layer; warm gold (amber) in inner layers, cold blue/silver in outer layers
- **Edges**: Laser-cut edges glow with backlight halos — visible paper fiber texture, physical cut thickness
- **Subjects**: All figures, animals, buildings rendered as flat cut silhouettes, depth created by layering
- **Transitions**: Each scene change = paper curtain peeling open to both sides like a theater drape, revealing the next layer's backlight glow. No hard cuts. No black. No page turns.
- **Camera**: Continuous dolly-in / push-in through layers; final reversal pull-back through all 5 layers closing the book

## Color Arc
- Outer (Clip 1–2): Cold blue, silver-white, midnight blue — moonlit forest
- Mid (Clip 3–4): Warm gold, amber, candlelight — train platform, Quidditch pitch, Great Hall
- Deep (Clip 5–6): Cold blue → warm gold → dark cover return

## Scenes

### Clip 1 — Book Opening → Forbidden Forest Layer 1 (00:00–00:08)
**First frame**: Closed standing book (@Image1), dark Gothic desk, candlelight rim-lighting the spine.
**00:00–00:03**: Vertical book on dark desk, cover facing forward, atmosphere dim and mysterious. Only ambient light traces the spine.
**00:03–00:08**: Book opens vertically — front and back cover spread apart like a diorama stage opening. First cardstock curtain unfurls from center outward. Moonlit Forbidden Forest emerges: layered paper clouds, paper tree branches, a folded-paper owl perched on a branch. Cold blue backlight illuminates from behind; silver-white glow halos the cloud and branch edges. Camera slowly pushes in toward layer 1 surface.
**Last frame**: Owl poised to take flight, cold blue backlight, paper edges glowing (@Image2).

### Clip 2 — Through Layer 1 → Platform Nine-and-Three-Quarters (00:08–00:16)
**First frame**: @Image2 — Owl on branch, cold blue glow.
**00:08–00:12**: Paper owl launches from branch, rigid paper wings fanning, trailing silver paper dust. First layer paper curtain gently peels open to both sides — paper trees and clouds grow transparent, warm yellow backlight seeps through the parting gap, second layer Nine-and-Three-Quarters platform glowing behind.
**00:12–00:16**: Camera fully enters second layer depth. Gothic arched colonnade silhouettes recede in perspective. Cardstock steam locomotive at mid-layer, warm yellow light pouring from cut-out windows and arches. Human silhouettes with luggage walk toward train. Remnant paper clouds from layer 1 float at foreground edges, reinforcing depth.
**Last frame**: Locomotive chimney billowing dense paper-scroll smoke, warm yellow light halos the smoke edges (@Image3).

### Clip 3 — Through Layer 2 → Quidditch Pitch (00:16–00:24)
**First frame**: @Image3 — Locomotive with paper smoke, warm amber glow.
**00:16–00:20**: Paper smoke fills layer 2. Second layer curtain peels open. Warm yellow transitions to fierce gold. Quidditch pitch emerges: ring-shaped stands receding in layers, Seeker silhouettes on brooms at mid-layer, Golden Snitch as a glowing cut-out paper orb. Camera pushes in.
**00:20–00:24**: Camera fully inside third layer. Ring stands in deep paper perspective. Seeker on paper broom dives, tail feathers rendered as laser-cut paper strips. Golden Snitch spins at high speed. Warm gold backlight from stands acts like stage spotlights. Camera continues push-in through paper goal hoops.
**Last frame**: Golden Snitch explodes into thousands of golden paper fragments flying toward lens (@Image4).

### Clip 4 — Through Layer 3 → Great Hall Montage (00:24–00:32)
**First frame**: @Image4 — Gold paper fragments suspended, gold light.
**00:24–00:28**: Gold paper fragments float and fall. Third layer curtain peels open. Fourth layer Great Hall glows with warm amber candlelight. Long tables recede in paper perspective; cut-out candle flames backlit amber through hollow silhouettes; paper stars hang from vaulted ceiling. Camera weaves between long tables.
**00:28–00:30**: Within same layer, scene shifts rapidly — long tables and candles fold down; Mirror of Erised rises (baroque mirror frame cut-out, warm light casting vague human silhouette within mirror); mirror folds away; Potions classroom rises (glass flasks as colored translucent cut-out paper, backlit in jewel tones).
**00:30–00:32**: All Potions elements reverse-unfold to flat plane, shatter into gold-and-white paper fragments, fragments sucked into a vortex pointing toward camera. Layer becomes transparent.
**Last frame**: Vortex of paper fragments at center, spiraling inward, faint light at vortex core (@Image5).

### Clip 5 — Through Layer 4 → Forbidden Forest Patronus (00:32–00:40)
**First frame**: @Image5 — Paper fragment vortex, cold light returning.
**00:32–00:36**: Vortex of fragments disperses. Fourth layer curtain peels open. Light shifts to cold blue-silver. Fifth layer deep Forbidden Forest glows: tall tree silhouettes recede in layers, cold blue backlight behind each trunk, eerie shadow-theater atmosphere. Paper web and paper spider silhouettes at foreground.
**00:36–00:40**: A folded-paper stag (Patronus) charges from mid-layer, silver-white backlight blazing from within its paper body. It crashes through foreground paper web; web fragments scatter in cold light. Stag continues charging toward camera, silver-white outline blazing like moonlight against deep blue.
**Last frame**: Stag shatters into hundreds of white paper cranes, flock launching toward camera then dispersing (@Image6).

### Clip 6 — Through Layer 5 → Hogwarts + All Layers Close (00:40–00:48)
**First frame**: @Image6 — Paper cranes dispersing, cold blue turning warm.
**00:40–00:43**: Paper cranes scatter. Fifth layer curtain peels open, revealing the deepest layer: Hogwarts Castle panorama. Castle towers, Forbidden Forest, Black Lake all rendered as massive layered cardstock silhouettes. Farthest back: fierce warm gold morning-light backlight, casting the entire castle as an epic silhouette. Camera lingers. Paper cranes fly over castle turrets.
**00:43–00:48**: Camera reverses — slow pull-back. Layer by layer, paper curtains close from innermost out: Layer 5 (Forbidden Forest) draws shut from both sides, Layer 4 (Great Hall) draws shut, Layer 3 (Quidditch) draws shut, Layer 2 (Platform) draws shut, Layer 1 (Forest) draws shut — each like a theater curtain closing. Book closes vertically, front and back covers fold together. Cover (@Image1) emits one warm gold pulse from gilded title, then fades to darkness. Final frame is identical to 00:00 opening frame — perfect loop.

## Music
48-second continuous orchestral score, no voice interference.
- **00:00–00:08**: Clear piano + strings, moonlit breeze, underscores book opening
- **00:08–00:16**: Warm light enters — viola + harp, rises with platform glow
- **00:16–00:24**: Fierce brass + timpani, golden energy with Quidditch push
- **00:24–00:30**: Warm woodwind + harpsichord, baroque warmth through Great Hall montage
- **00:30–00:40**: Full orchestra, epic sweep through forest and castle
- **00:40–00:48**: Decelerates — cello sustain + clear piano, paper curtains close one by one, volume fades to silence

**Music accent hits**: 3s (book opens), 10s (pass layer 1), 18s (pass layer 2), 26s (montage), 34s (pass layer 4), 42s (deepest layer), 45s (close begins)

## Sound Design
Book opening creak (thick cardboard friction), curtain peel (soft paper slide), owl wings (rigid paper fan), train steam (paper roll hiss), Snitch burst (paper ball pop + fragment flutter), layer transitions (continuous paper friction), stag charge (paper web shatter), paper crane flock (multi-layer cardboard wing chorus), book close (thick cardboard thud). All SFX mixed beneath music, never masking melody.

## Technical Requirements
- No text, letters, numbers, symbols, or subtitles anywhere in the video
- No voiceover
- Book stands vertical throughout; opens once at 00:00, closes once at 00:48
- All 6 clips connected via shared first/last frames (Clip N last = Clip N+1 first)
- Clip 1 first frame and Clip 6 last frame = @Image1 (perfect loop)
- Paper-cut light box aesthetic throughout: multi-layer cardstock silhouettes, independent backlighting per layer, physical paper texture and cut-edge depth
- Scene transitions via "paper curtain parting" — never hard cuts, never black screen
- Photorealistic paper craft quality: real cardstock volume, real backlight glow, real cast shadows, believable layered depth

# Harry Potter Paper-Cut Light Box — 48-Second Tunnel Book Film

## Concept
A 48-second cinematic loop built around a vertical tunnel book aesthetic. A real standing book opens once, reveals 5 layers of paper-cut diorama worlds, then closes. Each layer is a Harry Potter scene rendered in thick cardstock silhouettes with independent backlighting — warm gold, cold blue, amber — creating a shadow-box theater of depth and light. Six 8-second clips are stitched seamlessly via shared first/last frames. No text. No voiceover. Pure visual poetry.

## Visual Language
- **Medium**: Paper-cut light box / shadow box / vertical tunnel book
- **Layers**: 5–6 parallel heavy cardstock silhouette planes, 3–5 cm apart
- **Lighting**: Independent backlight behind each layer; warm gold (amber) in inner layers, cold blue/silver in outer layers
- **Edges**: Laser-cut edges glow with backlight halos — visible paper fiber texture, physical cut thickness
- **Subjects**: All figures, animals, buildings rendered as flat cut silhouettes, depth created by layering
- **Transitions**: Each scene change = paper curtain peeling open to both sides like a theater drape, revealing the next layer's backlight glow. No hard cuts. No black. No page turns.
- **Camera**: Continuous dolly-in / push-in through layers; final reversal pull-back through all 5 layers closing the book

## Color Arc
- Outer (Clip 1–2): Cold blue, silver-white, midnight blue — moonlit forest
- Mid (Clip 3–4): Warm gold, amber, candlelight — train platform, Quidditch pitch, Great Hall
- Deep (Clip 5–6): Cold blue → warm gold → dark cover return

## Scenes

### Clip 1 — Book Opening → Forbidden Forest Layer 1 (00:00–00:08)
**First frame**: Closed standing book (@Image1), dark Gothic desk, candlelight rim-lighting the spine.
**00:00–00:03**: Vertical book on dark desk, cover facing forward, atmosphere dim and mysterious. Only ambient light traces the spine.
**00:03–00:08**: Book opens vertically — front and back cover spread apart like a diorama stage opening. First cardstock curtain unfurls from center outward. Moonlit Forbidden Forest emerges: layered paper clouds, paper tree branches, a folded-paper owl perched on a branch. Cold blue backlight illuminates from behind; silver-white glow halos the cloud and branch edges. Camera slowly pushes in toward layer 1 surface.
**Last frame**: Owl poised to take flight, cold blue backlight, paper edges glowing (@Image2).

### Clip 2 — Through Layer 1 → Platform Nine-and-Three-Quarters (00:08–00:16)
**First frame**: @Image2 — Owl on branch, cold blue glow.
**00:08–00:12**: Paper owl launches from branch, rigid paper wings fanning, trailing silver paper dust. First layer paper curtain gently peels open to both sides — paper trees and clouds grow transparent, warm yellow backlight seeps through the parting gap, second layer Nine-and-Three-Quarters platform glowing behind.
**00:12–00:16**: Camera fully enters second layer depth. Gothic arched colonnade silhouettes recede in perspective. Cardstock steam locomotive at mid-layer, warm yellow light pouring from cut-out windows and arches. Human silhouettes with luggage walk toward train. Remnant paper clouds from layer 1 float at foreground edges, reinforcing depth.
**Last frame**: Locomotive chimney billowing dense paper-scroll smoke, warm yellow light halos the smoke edges (@Image3).

### Clip 3 — Through Layer 2 → Quidditch Pitch (00:16–00:24)
**First frame**: @Image3 — Locomotive with paper smoke, warm amber glow.
**00:16–00:20**: Paper smoke fills layer 2. Second layer curtain peels open. Warm yellow transitions to fierce gold. Quidditch pitch emerges: ring-shaped stands receding in layers, Seeker silhouettes on brooms at mid-layer, Golden Snitch as a glowing cut-out paper orb. Camera pushes in.
**00:20–00:24**: Camera fully inside third layer. Ring stands in deep paper perspective. Seeker on paper broom dives, tail feathers rendered as laser-cut paper strips. Golden Snitch spins at high speed. Warm gold backlight from stands acts like stage spotlights. Camera continues push-in through paper goal hoops.
**Last frame**: Golden Snitch explodes into thousands of golden paper fragments flying toward lens (@Image4).

### Clip 4 — Through Layer 3 → Great Hall Montage (00:24–00:32)
**First frame**: @Image4 — Gold paper fragments suspended, gold light.
**00:24–00:28**: Gold paper fragments float and fall. Third layer curtain peels open. Fourth layer Great Hall glows with warm amber candlelight. Long tables recede in paper perspective; cut-out candle flames backlit amber through hollow silhouettes; paper stars hang from vaulted ceiling. Camera weaves between long tables.
**00:28–00:30**: Within same layer, scene shifts rapidly — long tables and candles fold down; Mirror of Erised rises (baroque mirror frame cut-out, warm light casting vague human silhouette within mirror); mirror folds away; Potions classroom rises (glass flasks as colored translucent cut-out paper, backlit in jewel tones).
**00:30–00:32**: All Potions elements reverse-unfold to flat plane, shatter into gold-and-white paper fragments, fragments sucked into a vortex pointing toward camera. Layer becomes transparent.
**Last frame**: Vortex of paper fragments at center, spiraling inward, faint light at vortex core (@Image5).

### Clip 5 — Through Layer 4 → Forbidden Forest Patronus (00:32–00:40)
**First frame**: @Image5 — Paper fragment vortex, cold light returning.
**00:32–00:36**: Vortex of fragments disperses. Fourth layer curtain peels open. Light shifts to cold blue-silver. Fifth layer deep Forbidden Forest glows: tall tree silhouettes recede in layers, cold blue backlight behind each trunk, eerie shadow-theater atmosphere. Paper web and paper spider silhouettes at foreground.
**00:36–00:40**: A folded-paper stag (Patronus) charges from mid-layer, silver-white backlight blazing from within its paper body. It crashes through foreground paper web; web fragments scatter in cold light. Stag continues charging toward camera, silver-white outline blazing like moonlight against deep blue.
**Last frame**: Stag shatters into hundreds of white paper cranes, flock launching toward camera then dispersing (@Image6).

### Clip 6 — Through Layer 5 → Hogwarts + All Layers Close (00:40–00:48)
**First frame**: @Image6 — Paper cranes dispersing, cold blue turning warm.
**00:40–00:43**: Paper cranes scatter. Fifth layer curtain peels open, revealing the deepest layer: Hogwarts Castle panorama. Castle towers, Forbidden Forest, Black Lake all rendered as massive layered cardstock silhouettes. Farthest back: fierce warm gold morning-light backlight, casting the entire castle as an epic silhouette. Camera lingers. Paper cranes fly over castle turrets.
**00:43–00:48**: Camera reverses — slow pull-back. Layer by layer, paper curtains close from innermost out: Layer 5 (Forbidden Forest) draws shut from both sides, Layer 4 (Great Hall) draws shut, Layer 3 (Quidditch) draws shut, Layer 2 (Platform) draws shut, Layer 1 (Forest) draws shut — each like a theater curtain closing. Book closes vertically, front and back covers fold together. Cover (@Image1) emits one warm gold pulse from gilded title, then fades to darkness. Final frame is identical to 00:00 opening frame — perfect loop.

## Music
48-second continuous orchestral score, no voice interference.
- **00:00–00:08**: Clear piano + strings, moonlit breeze, underscores book opening
- **00:08–00:16**: Warm light enters — viola + harp, rises with platform glow
- **00:16–00:24**: Fierce brass + timpani, golden energy with Quidditch push
- **00:24–00:30**: Warm woodwind + harpsichord, baroque warmth through Great Hall montage
- **00:30–00:40**: Full orchestra, epic sweep through forest and castle
- **00:40–00:48**: Decelerates — cello sustain + clear piano, paper curtains close one by one, volume fades to silence

**Music accent hits**: 3s (book opens), 10s (pass layer 1), 18s (pass layer 2), 26s (montage), 34s (pass layer 4), 42s (deepest layer), 45s (close begins)

## Sound Design
Book opening creak (thick cardboard friction), curtain peel (soft paper slide), owl wings (rigid paper fan), train steam (paper roll hiss), Snitch burst (paper ball pop + fragment flutter), layer transitions (continuous paper friction), stag charge (paper web shatter), paper crane flock (multi-layer cardboard wing chorus), book close (thick cardboard thud). All SFX mixed beneath music, never masking melody.

## Technical Requirements
- No text, letters, numbers, symbols, or subtitles anywhere in the video
- No voiceover
- Book stands vertical throughout; opens once at 00:00, closes once at 00:48
- All 6 clips connected via shared first/last frames (Clip N last = Clip N+1 first)
- Clip 1 first frame and Clip 6 last frame = @Image1 (perfect loop)
- Paper-cut light box aesthetic throughout: multi-layer cardstock silhouettes, independent backlighting per layer, physical paper texture and cut-edge depth
- Scene transitions via "paper curtain parting" — never hard cuts, never black screen
- Photorealistic paper craft quality: real cardstock volume, real backlight glow, real cast shadows, believable layered depth

完美——British Warwick 这个深沉史诗感正好配这部安利片。现在规划**音画精确对位台词**：

**时间轴对位逻辑：**
| Clip | 时间 | 时长 | 画面内容 | 台词 |
|------|------|------|---------|------|
| 1 | 0–5.1s | 5.1s | 书本在暗处，封面亮起，右翻打开，禁林纸幕亮起 | 开篇悬念 |
| 2 | 5.1–13.1s | 8s | 猫头鹰飞起，穿过第一层，站台火车登场 | 魔法世界入口 |
| 3 | 13.1–21.2s | 8s | 穿过烟雾，魁地奇球场金光炽烈 | 冒险与荣耀 |
| 4 | 21.2–26.3s | 5.1s | 大礼堂烛光，纸屑漩涡 | 归属与魔法 |

C2V是什么

C2V 是 **CSS-to-Video** 的简称——您在请求里粘贴了 CSS 动画代码，意思是希望按照这份 CSS 定义的动画效果（圆环展开、图例滑入、数字淡入等）生成对应的视频。

实现方式是把 CSS 动画逻辑翻译成视频生成提示词，然后用 T2V（文字生视频）或 I2V（图片生视频）来实现，并不是一个独立的技术术语或工具——是您这个需求场景下的说法。

## 【第五步：TTS 配音】（British Warwick 音色）

**台词设计原则：**
```
- 每段台词时长 ≤ 对应clip时长 × 80%
- 从clip开始后约200-500ms放置
- 风格：极简、悬念感、电影感，每句不超过10个英文单词
- 每句对应一个画面事件，而非描述画面

模板（6段结构）：
Clip1（封面开启）："[一句引入悬念的话，暗示书的核心主题]"
Clip2（第一层场景）："[书中第一个标志性元素] [简短动作/状态]."
Clip3（第二层场景）："[核心冲突/高潮元素]. [情绪词]."  
Clip4（第三层场景）："[书中最温暖/最重要的场景]. [一个感受词]."
Clip5（第四层场景）："[书中最震撼的意象]. [节奏感强的3个短句]."
Clip6（收尾））："Every time you open this book — [书给读者的核心价值]."
```
